case_name: G. Ramamoorthy vs The State Of Karnataka

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Karnataka, Indiranagar Police Station, and MS. SANDHYA MAHESH

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Marriage between son of the petitioner and respondent No.2 came to be solemnized on 31.05.2012. Respondent No.2 filed a petition for divorce alleging misleading facts, demand for dowry, and harassment.

legal_principles.principle: A complaint cannot be read in isolation and has to be read along with allegations made in other related complaints.
legal_principles.held: averments made in the complaint cannot be read in isolation and it has to be read along with allegations made in M.C.No.448/2014

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to quash a FIR to show that the allegations are false and that the police have no jurisdiction.
legal_principles.held: He would also contend that all overt-acts alleged to have been made by petitioner has taken place at Ambur, Vellore District, Bengaluru and as such, false complaint against the petitioner has been filed at Bengaluru
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

outcome.final_order: The FIR registered against the petitioner/accused No.2 is quashed.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing a FIR under Section 482 CR.P.C.
